name: Comet Dial
description: A rotary dial with a comet tail: the arc fills by dragging, the indicator head leaves fading particles behind, and the number sits in the middle in fixed-width Persian digits.
interactionNotes: Press and drag around the circle to change the value; releasing with speed gives momentum, and a spring settles the value onto the nearest step with a slight bounce. In RTL zero is on the right and the value increases toward the left; in LTR it is the reverse. The arrow keys work too — in RTL `ArrowLeft` increases.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value in the uncontrolled state.

props.name: unit
props.description: The unit next to the number; an empty string means no unit.

props.name: speed
props.description: Speed of the number spring, 0 to 100.

props.name: tapBounce
props.description: Spring bounce on a tap (0 to 0.9).

props.name: flickBounce
props.description: Spring bounce on a flick (0 to 0.9).

props.name: onChangeEnd
props.type: (value: number, detail: { velocity: number; bounce: number }) => void
props.description: When the motion ends; it also reports velocity and bounce.

tips: Zero is on the right in RTL and the value increases toward the left — the Persian convention. This mirroring happens in JS, so it is enough for the page to be `dir="rtl"`; no `rtl` prop is needed.

Digits render as Persian and each one sits in a fixed-width 0.694em box; `tabular-nums` has no effect with the Peyda font, and these boxes are the only thing keeping the number from shaking while it turns.
For a unit other than percent, change `unit` — `°`, `dB`, or an empty string. An empty string means just the number, and the number stays centered on its own.
`onChangeEnd` is the right place to save to the server: it is not called on every drag frame, only once the spring has settled.
